title: Derivations act on perfect complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $D(R)$ be its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $\delta:R	o R$ be additive with $\delta(rs)=\delta(r)s+r\delta(s)$. Write $\iota:\operatorname{Perf}(R)	o D(R)$ for the full inclusion of perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. There is a natural transformation $\eta:\iota	o\iota[1]$ with the following property. For every bounded complex $A$ of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and every family of additive maps $
abla^i:A^i	o A^i$ satisfying $
abla^i(rm)=\delta(r)m+r
abla^i(m)$, there is a chain map $f:A	o A[1]$ whose component, identified with a map $A^i	o A^{i+1}$, is $
abla^{i+1}d^i-d^i
abla^i$, and $\eta_{Q(A)}=Q(f)c_{Q,1,A}$, where $c_{Q,1,A}:Q(A[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(A)[1]$ is the localization shift comparison.

proof.text: Split each projective module from a free module and differentiate its coordinates to construct a connection. Leibniz makes the commutator linear; d squared zero makes it a cocycle. The map commutator for each chain map is a boundary witnessing naturality, including independence of connections.

Bounded projective models are K-projective, so represent derived maps by chain maps. Choose a perfect model for each object and conjugate its commutator class along the model isomorphism. Naturality for represented maps gives naturality on the full subcategory and the formula for every model and connection.
